subject: Finex — bake-off synthesis and action plan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Hayes <daniel.hayes@finex.com>, Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@finex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Finex — post-demo notes & proposed next steps

Hi Daniel / Aisha,

Thanks again for your time today. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can move the bake-off to the technical phase.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency variability on long-tail queries (p95 spikes during peak business hours)
- High per-token inference cost for interactive features
- Data residency and audit trail requirements for EU customer records

Goals (what success looks like)
- 40%+ reduction in inference unit cost for conversational flows
- p50 < 150ms and p95 < 400ms for 1k concurrent requests in EU region
- SOC 2 evidence + audit log retention for 12 months

What we covered
- Demo of Redwood inference runtime and autoscaling
- Prefix caching examples and expected cost impacts
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for throughput and data isolation

Open questions / info requested
1) We'll provide a pricing worksheet (attached) with dedicated vs hosted scenarios.
2) Please share your decision criteria spreadsheet — we can map test plan to each line.
3) We recommend a 3-day vendor-staged bake-off: peak simulation + accuracy regression checks.

Attachments
- [Attachment: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)]

Proposed next steps
- Priyom to share pricing sheet and proposed test plan by EOD tomorrow (Jan 13)
- Finex to share decision criteria + access to anonymized test corpus by Jan 18
- Schedule technical deep-dive with infra team the week of Jan 19 (Ben + Marissa)

Would Tues 1/20 10:00am PT work for the technical deep-dive? If not, propose two slots.

Thanks,

Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Finex — post-demo notes & proposed next steps

Priyom,

Quick notes — agree with the ask. A couple additions for the test plan:
- Include a 0-100 token distribution sweep and a separate long-context (>1024 tokens) run
- Measure KV cache hit rates and end-to-end p95 with and without prefix caching
- Add a simple cost-projection sheet for 6/12/24 month horizons

I drafted a short scoring rubric (attached) so we can rank vendors on latency/cost/ops.

On Tue 1/20 10:00am PT — I can take that slot and will invite runtime eng + SRE.

-ben

Subject: Finex bake-off plan & competitive points — internal

Team,

Finex confirmed decision criteria and shared the test corpus (received yesterday). Short internal plan and next steps before the deep-dive today at 10am PT (invite sent):

1) Test harness
- Run three staged tests: baseline latency sweep, peak concurrency (1k reqs), accuracy/regression checks
- Use provided corpus (anonymized). Ben to own harness and run on dedicated nodes.

2) Scoring
- Use rubric Ben drafted (latency/cost/security/ops). We'll map to Finex workbook.
- I'll prepare vendor comparison template; baseline competitors include VendorX (open quant) and VendorY (managed) — note: avoid naming in customer docs until asked.

3) Deliverables
- Run initial perf test by 1/23, share raw results and cost projection by 1/26
- SOC2 evidence and audit log export: Marissa to own and provide link to secure share
- Customer-facing vendor comparison and test plan: Priyom to send by EOD 1/21
